newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westpac Australia consumer index falls in Oct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westpac Australia consumer index falls in Oct.

text.p: The Westpac/Melbourne Institute consumer sentiment index for October fell 4.1 points, or 3.9 percent to 101.4.
The index has now fallen 9.2 percent from its post-election peak in March and back to its lowest level since October 1995.

"The major factor in the decline in consumer sentiment is a decline in confidence about economic propects. Confidence about the economy over the next 12 months declined 7.1 percent and is now 21.8 percent below its March peak," said Westpac's General Manager, economics, Bill Evans.

"The fall in the consumer sentiment index has occured since June and oddly coincides with a period of falling interest rates," Evans said, noting that this would normally lead to a rise in confidence, as in the early 1990's.
But he added that uncertainty about employment, heightened by the rise in unemployment in recent months, is clearly the over-riding influence.
"The case for the Reserve Bank to cut interest rates in early November is strengthened by this development. A rate cut would help to stem the slide in confidence," Evans said.
Consumer confidence fell in all states with the exception of Tasmania, although while showing a rise the state still recorded the lowest level of confidence with an index level of 82.7.

Western Australia (WA), Victoria and New South Wales all recorded index readings above 100, while confidence was below average in Queensland at 99.6 and South Australia at 98.7, which along with WA, suffered the sharpest falls in the month.
